assumptions: Node.js environment is available on the local machine
The game logic can be implemented entirely in JavaScript/TypeScript
Canvas/WebGL is sufficient for the required visual effects
Simple commodity market price variation algorithms are acceptable
Pirate AI can be basic and still provide engaging combat
discoveryProposalPayload.candidate_scope: Minimum useful scope: a playable browser-based game with at least 8 star systems, one station per system, a simple commodity trading market, basic hyperspace travel (fuel consumption, pirate encounters), ship-to-ship combat (player lasers vs AI), ship upgrades (cargo, laser, shields, fuel), and save/load functionality. The frontend must be a single-page canvas/WebGL application with visual effects (parallax starfield, hyperspace jump, laser combat), and the server must expose a /healthz endpoint.

discoveryProposalPayload.problem_statement: A desire exists to create an Elite-inspired single-player space trading and combat game playable in a web browser. The game should deliver a complete single-page experience with parallax starfield, hyperspace jumps, station docking, ship management (shields, fuel, cargo, credits), commodity trading with dynamic pricing, and arcade laser combat with visual effects.
discoveryProposalPayload.rationale: The initiative is well-bounded with clear constraints and a specific technology stack (Node.js server, Chrome frontend, TypeScript, no external dependencies). The scope is appropriate for XS complexity, and the functional requirements are understood (8+ systems, trading, combat, upgrades, save/load). Visual polish expectations are reasonable for a browser-based game. The verification requirements (unit tests, browser smoke test, /healthz) are standard and achievable. No evidence suggests technical infeasibility or missing critical information.

inputSnapshot.initiativeSubject: Elite-style single-player space trading and combat game with a rich browser frontend played in Google Chrome. A local Node.js server serves the game; the player opens http://localhost:<port> in Chrome and plays immediately (npm install && npm start, no manual build steps). The frontend is a first-class acceptance subject: a beautiful single-page canvas/WebGL application with a parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effect, station docking screen, ship HUD (shields, fuel, cargo, credits), commodity market screen with dynamic prices, and arcade laser combat with visual effects. Core gameplay loop: start docked at a station with 100 credits and a small cargo hold; buy low / sell high across a galaxy of at least 8 named systems with per-system price variation; hyperspace jumps consume fuel and carry pirate-encounter risk; win ship-to-ship combat (player lasers vs enemy AI) or flee; spend profits on ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank); progress toward the Elite rating tracked by profit and combat kills; save/load the game state. Non-functional: 60fps target on a 2020 laptop in Chrome, no external CDN dependencies (fully offline), English UI. Testing: unit tests for market pricing, jump/fuel math, combat resolution and save/load; a browser smoke test that loads the page and asserts the canvas renders; the server must expose /healthz.
